newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY, GE SIGN OFFSET AHEAD OF PLANE TENDER.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY, GE SIGN OFFSET AHEAD OF PLANE TENDER.

text.p: Hungary announced on Friday the signing with General Electric Trading of an offset agreement worth hundreds of millions of dollars, linked to the country's planned military aircraft purchases.

"The offset agreement opens new perspectives for industrial cooperation in various sectors such as electronics, software, financial investments, aircraft emgine production," industry minister Szabolcs Fazakas said.
Hungary, one of the frontrunner countries for NATO membership in the next few years, plans to update its air force, currently made up of ageing Soviet-built aircraft.
McDonnell Douglas is coordinating with GE in competing for post-Cold War business in Hungary against Saab of Sweden, which makes the Gripen, Lockheed Martin's F-16, French Dassault 's "Mirage".
Russia's state arms agency Rosvooruzhenie was also reported earlier this week to be considering offering Su-27s, Su-30s and fourth generation Su-39s.

GE, the largest aircraft engine producer of the world, makes the engines for the F-18, and also supplies F-16s and Gripens, but is collaborating most closely with McDonnell Douglas in its efforts to sell to Hungary.

Imre Mecs, chairman of the Hungarian parliament's defence committee told reporters the Hungarian government was likely to decide on publishing a tender for new fighters following the NATO's Madrid summit in July.
The summit is expected to invite Hungary and a small group of other Central European countries to become members of the alliance.
"We will be able to estimate what requirements we should meet within NATO following (the summit), he said.
Defence ministry sources said last year that Hungary -- depending on the timescale of its hoped-for NATO membership -- is looking to buy some 30 fighters.
Offset agreements with the producers may be decisive factors when Hungary evaluates the bids for the aircraft tender, Fazakas said.
"In selecting the winner, it will be a serious factor what offset facilities (the bidders) are able to bring," he said.
Hungary has already concluded offset agreements with McDonnell Douglas, Lockheed Martin and SAAB.

Hungary expects GE, which has already invested more than $700 hundred million in the country, to help Hungary increase its exports to the U.S. with technological support, investment and marketing, Fazakas said.
He added that the final amount to be covered by the offset agreement would depend on how many aircraft and spare parts Hungary would buy.

GE Trading President and CEO Stuart A. Fisher said GE Trading, GE Company's vehicle to complete offset obligations, had major programmes in several European countries such as Finland, Switzerland, Sweden, Spain and Turkey.
